extracted.intended_audience: developers and implementers of MathML renderers, editors, tools, and authors encoding mathematics for the Web
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative rules for implementing, authoring, transferring, and validating MathML 4.0 (MathML Full) including Presentation and Content markup, accessibility annotations, parsing/validation, and conformance testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended readership and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: This specification ... is intended primarily for a readership consisting of those who will be developing or implementing renderers or editors using it, or software that will communicate using MathML as a protocol for input or output. It is not a User's Guide but rather a reference document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should treat this document as a reference for correct behavior of renderers, editors and converters rather than as a tutorial for authors; use additional notes and non-normative 'Notes on MathML' for best-practice examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation vs Content markup
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptually, MathML consists of two main strains of markup: Presentation markup is used to display mathematical expressions; and Content markup is used to convey mathematical meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Presentation markup when the goal is visual rendering, Content markup when expressing semantic structure for computation or accessibility; both can be combined using parallel markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML namespace requirement and recommended form
rubrics_metrics.description: The URI for the MathML namespace is: http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML. If a MathML expression is likely to be in contexts where it may be parsed by an XML parser or an HTML parser, it SHOULD use the following form to ensure maximum compatibility: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> ... </math>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authoring MathML, include the namespace declaration on the top-level math element to maximize compatibility across XML and HTML parsers; do not use prefixed element names in HTML serialisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar and schema formalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules for allowed elements, the order in which they can appear, and how they may be contained within each other ... are defined by this specification, and formalized by a RelaxNG schema in A. Parsing MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers should validate MathML using the provided RelaxNG schema (and optional DTD/XML Schema derivatives) to ensure syntactic conformance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute value syntaxes and types
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe the MathML-specific syntax of attribute values, the following conventions and notations are used for most attributes ... boolean, unsigned-integer, positive-integer, integer, number, unsigned-number, character, string, length, color, id, idref, URI, italicized word, 'literal', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and parse attribute values according to the specified syntactic types; respect the notation operators (?, *, +, sequencing, alternatives) when interpreting composite attribute forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII case-insensitive comparison for enumerated attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: For compatibility with HTML, attributes defined with an enumerated list of string values are to be compared as ASCII case-insensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When checking enumerated attribute values, convert to ASCII-case-insensitive form before comparison (e.g., 'True', 'true', 'TRUE' equivalent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length-valued attributes and namedspace tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Most presentation elements have attributes that accept values representing lengths ... MathML Core accepts lengths only in the <length-percentage> syntax defined in CSS; MathML Full extends length syntax by accepting also a namedspace being an ASCII case-insensitive match to one of: veryverythinmathspace, negativeveryverythinmathspace, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support CSS length/percentage units and the listed namedspace tokens; treat MathML Full namedspace tokens case-insensitively and map them to the specified em-based values where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default attribute values: inherited vs automatic vs computed
rubrics_metrics.description: Default values described as inherited are taken from the rendering environment ... Default values described as automatic should be computed by a MathML renderer in a way which will produce a high-quality rendering; how to do this is not usually specified by the MathML specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers must implement inheritance semantics, compute 'automatic' defaults to produce acceptable rendering quality, and apply mstyle to change defaults for children; explicit words 'inherited' or 'automatic' are not permitted as literal attribute values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace handling and normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML ignores whitespace occurring outside token elements. Whitespace occurring within the content of token elements ... is normalized: leading and trailing whitespace removed, and internal sequences collapsed to a single space. Authors wishing to encode whitespace at start or end must use non-breaking space U+00A0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement parsers/renderers to trim and collapse whitespace in token content; preserve explicit non-breaking spaces if author intended them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes allowed on every MathML element
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to attributes described specifically for each element, the attributes in the following table are allowed on every MathML element: id, xref, class, style, href, intent, arg ... xml:lang and attributes from other namespaces which are ignored by default are also allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support the listed global attributes and ignore unknown non-MathML-namespaced attributes by default; implement id/xref linking for parallel markup and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: intent and arg attributes for annotating intent
rubrics_metrics.description: All MathML presentation elements accept intent and arg attributes to support specifying intent. The intent attribute ... may be used on presentation elements to give information about the intended meaning of the expression, mainly for guiding audio or braille accessible renderings. The arg attribute may be used to name an element to be referenced from an intent expression on an ancestor element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement intent and arg parsing and evaluation to improve accessibility renderings; authors should use intent/arg to convey semantic hints for non-sighted renditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathML Core vs MathML Full relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML Core covers (most of) Presentation Markup, with the focus being the precise details of displaying mathematics in web browsers. MathML Full, this specification, extends MathML Core primarily by defining Content MathML ... It is intended that MathML Full is a proper superset of MathML Core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure implementations claiming MathML Core compatibility at least implement Core features; Full implementations must include Content MathML features and Full-only attributes described in this spec.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering recommendations and renderer discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Web Platform implementations of [MathML-Core] should follow the detailed layout rules specified in that document. This document only recommends (i.e., does not require) specific ways of rendering Presentation MathML; this is in order to allow for medium-dependent rendering and for implementations not using the CSS based Web Platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MathML-Core layout rules where applicable; allow renderer-specific strategies for medium-dependent rendering while ensuring semantic and accessibility requirements are maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsing/validation methods (RelaxNG/DTD/XML Schema)
rubrics_metrics.description: These rules are defined by this specification, and formalized by a RelaxNG schema in A. Parsing MathML. Derived schema in other formats, DTD (Document Type Definition) and XML Schema are also provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate MathML using the provided RelaxNG schema or the derived DTD/XML Schema as appropriate; use appendix A as authoritative for parsing/validation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining MathML with other formats and host environment interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: This specification addresses how MathML renderers might be implemented and should interact with browsers ... sections on mixing MathML and XHTML, mixing MathML and non-XML contexts, mixing MathML and HTML, Linking, MathML and Graphical Markup, and Using CSS with MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement robust embedding rules for HTML/XHTML contexts, support annotation-xml in HTML documents where specified, respect CSS interaction guidance and the specified order of processing attributes vs style sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring MathML and recommended behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: 7.3 Transferring MathML and 7.3.2 Recommended Behaviors when Transferring discuss resource types for MathML documents and recommended behaviors when transferring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the recommended transfer behaviors (media types, encodings, and representation choices) to maximize interoperability between applications and avoid corruption of MathML content in transit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel markup and semantics annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections discuss Combining Presentation and Content Markup, The <semantics> element, The <annotation> element, and Parallel Markup via Cross-References. Parallel markup allows Presentation, Content and other formats to be combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use <semantics> with appropriate <annotation> and <annotation-xml> children to provide alternate or parallel semantic representations; implement cross-referenced parallel markup for richer accessibility and computational uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content MathML: strict versus non-strict uses and content dictionaries
rubrics_metrics.description: 4.1.5 Strict Content MathML, 4.1.6 Content Dictionaries, and many content element sections describe strict and non-strict uses of <cn>, <ci>, <csymbol>, <apply>, <bind>, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Strict Content MathML semantics where required, provide mechanisms for content dictionaries, and follow the transformation rules in F. (The Strict Content MathML Transformation) when normalizing non-strict content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict Content MathML transformation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: F. The Strict Content MathML Transformation lists rewrite rules: rewrite non-strict bind, idiomatic qualifiers (derivatives, integrals, limits, sums/products, roots, logarithms, moments), normalize container markup, eliminate domainofapplication, rewrite token elements, operators, attributes, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers converting or normalizing MathML content should apply the F. transformation steps to produce Strict Content MathML canonical forms for consistent semantic processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator dictionary and default operator behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a MathML operator dictionary used as a source of global default values for behavior in rendering MathML ... B. Operator Dictionary provides examples and a default example is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult and implement the operator dictionary for default spacing, stretching and other operator-related defaults; allow implementations to consult dictionary entries when computing presentation behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linebreaking of expressions and control attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: 3.1.7 Linebreaking of Expressions, 3.1.7.1 Control of Linebreaks, 3.1.7.2 Examples of Linebreaking and various linebreaking attributes are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect linebreaking attributes and control rules when rendering multi-line math; provide reasonable default linebreakstyles and expose attributes for authors to control linebreaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token elements and required arguments rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 3.2 Token Elements and 3.1.3 Required Arguments describe token elements (<mi>, <mn>, <mo>, <mtext>, <ms>, <mspace/>, <mglyph/>) and the argument requirements for presentation elements (including inferred <mrow>s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure token elements validate their content rules (e.g., numbers not to be written using <mn> alone in some cases), implement inferred <mrow> behavior when variadic children are used where a single argument is conceptually required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility guidance for content authors
rubrics_metrics.description: C. MathML Accessibility includes C.4 Content Authors with Overarching guidance: Always use markup; Use intent and arg attributes; and Specific Markup Guidance on invisible operators, proper grouping, spacing, numbers, superscripts/subscripts, elementary math, tables and lists, natural-language mathematics, accessible descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prefer semantic markup and intent annotations to improve audio/braille renderings; implementers should expose and honor intent/arg and provide accessible descriptions derived from markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance, test suite, and deprecated features
rubrics_metrics.description: D.1 MathML Conformance, D.1.1 MathML Test Suite and Validator, D.1.2 Deprecated MathML 1.x and MathML 2.x Features, and D.1.3 MathML Extension Mechanisms and Conformance discuss what constitutes conformance and testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official test suite and validator to verify conformance; be aware of deprecated constructs and documented extension mechanisms and their implications for conformance claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error handling and recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: D.2 Handling of Errors and other sections (e.g., intent Error Handling) describe how errors should be handled, error markup (<cerror>), and recovery strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement graceful error handling strategies: validate where possible, emit <cerror> for unrepresentable content, and provide error-recovery behaviors as specified to avoid loss of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and privacy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: D.4 Privacy Considerations and D.5 Security Considerations list privacy and security implications of MathML usage in host environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and mitigate privacy/security risks when transferring/embedding MathML (e.g., external resources via href/annotation-xml), follow the spec's guidance to avoid security pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of annotation elements and alternate representations
rubrics_metrics.description: 6.1 Annotation keys, 6.2 Alternate representations, 6.3 Content equivalents, 6.5 The <semantics> element, 6.6 The <annotation> element, 6.7 The <annotation-xml> element describe annotation mechanisms for alternate or machine-readable representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide annotations for alternate encodings (e.g., LaTeX, MathML Content strings, JSON-LD) inside <semantics> to enable interoperability and richer processing by consuming applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsing tolerances and normalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification notes that whitespace normalization, allowable numerical attribute rounding by renderers, and other normalization behaviors (e.g., handling numeric values outside sensible ranges) should be applied by processing applications; HTML compatibility requires certain behaviors (e.g., ignoring xmlns attribute when parsing as HTML).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement robust normalization: trim/collapse whitespace as specified, round numerical values to sensible renderer-supported subsets, and follow HTML-vs-XML parsing compatibility notes to maximize interoperability.
